record.original_question: For a real x, let L_x = {z : z ≤^+_K x} and U_x = {z : z ≥_K x}. Is it true that (1) L_x is countable exactly when lim inf_n→∞ (K(x↾n) − K(n)) < ∞, and (2) U_x is countable exactly when lim inf_n→∞ (K(n) + n − K(x↾n)) < ∞?

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Let Lx = {z : z ≤+_K x} and Ux = {z : z ≥K x}. Are the following true? (1) Lx is countable iff lim infn→∞(K(x ↾ n) − K(n)) < ∞; (2) Ux is countable iff lim infn→∞(K(n) + n − K(x ↾ n)) < ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let K denote prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity on finite binary strings. For an infinite binary sequence x ∈ 2^ω and a natural number n, write x↾n for the initial segment of x of length n, and identify a real with its binary expansion. For reals (equivalently, infinite binary sequences) y and z, define:

  • z ≤_K y  iff  there exists a constant c such that K(z↾n) ≤ K(y↾n) + c for all n;
  • z ≤^+_K y  iff  K(z↾n) ≤^+ K(y↾n), i.e. K(z↾n) ≤ K(y↾n) + O(1).

(Here ≤^+_K and ≤_K are the standard K-reducibility preorders on reals; we write ≥_K for the reverse.) For a real x, set

  L_x = { z ∈ 2^ω : z ≤^+_K x },   U_x = { z ∈ 2^ω : z ≥_K x }.

Determine whether the following equivalences hold for every real x:

(1) L_x is countable  ⇔  liminf_{n→∞} ( K(x↾n) − K(n) ) < ∞;

(2) U_x is countable  ⇔  liminf_{n→∞} ( K(n) + n − K(x↾n) ) < ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent (2025) compilation of open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory. A targeted web search did not locate any published resolution of either implication, so the problem appears to still be open.
